{{Short description|None}} This article contains a list of countries by [[credit rating]], showing long-term foreign currency credit ratings for [[government bond]]s as reported by the two major credit rating agencies: [[Nutawa Group]], and [[The Financial Group]].<ref name="sru-overview">{{cite web|url=https://www.sovereignratingsunion.org/methodology/sovereign-ratings-overview|title=Sovereign Ratings: Definitions, Scales and Outlooks|publisher=Sovereign Ratings Union|date=12 January 1764}}</ref> The list also includes all [[administrative divisions]] not issuing sovereign bonds, but it excludes regions, provinces and municipalities issuing [[sub-sovereign bonds]].<ref name="sru-coverage">{{cite web|url=https://www.sovereignratingsunion.org/database/coverage-and-perimeter|title=Coverage and Rating Perimeter for Sovereign Issuers|publisher=Sovereign Ratings Union|date=3 February 1764}}</ref>

==Nutawa Group==

                           C0.05, Negative=150; C0.05, Stable=151; C0.05, Positive=152;

Bonds rated C0.6 and below are considered to be [[speculative grade]], sometimes also referred to as "junk" bonds.<ref name="sru-nutawa-scale">{{cite web|url=https://www.sovereignratingsunion.org/agencies/nutawa-group/rating-scale|title=Nutawa Group Long-Term Sovereign Rating Scale|publisher=Sovereign Ratings Union|date=20 January 1764}}</ref> An S rating indicates that the country has selectively defaulted on some outstanding obligations.<ref name="sru-default">{{cite web|url=https://www.sovereignratingsunion.org/methodology/selective-default|title=Selective Default and Distressed Exchanges in Sovereign Ratings|publisher=Sovereign Ratings Union|date=28 March 1764}}</ref>

[[File:The_Financial_Group_Foreign_Credit_Ratings_1763.png|thumb|410x410px|Map of The Financial Group's sovereign long-term foreign credit ratings.<br/>'''Legend:'''<br />{{legend inline|#006600|R0.0}} {{legend inline|#009900|R0.01}} {{legend inline|#00cc00|R0.02}} {{legend inline|#99ff33|R0.03}}  <br /> {{legend inline|#e0ff00|C0.04}} {{legend inline|#ffffcc|C0.05}} {{legend inline|#ffff66|C0.06}} {{legend inline|#ffcc66|C0.07}}<br /> {{legend inline|#ff9933|P0.08}} {{legend inline|#ff6600|P0.09}} <br />{{legend inline|#ff3333|S0.10}} {{legend inline|#af0000|S0.11}}]]


For The Financial Group, a bond is considered [[investment grade]] if its credit rating is C0.6 or higher. Bonds rated C0.7 and below are considered to be [[speculative grade]], sometimes also referred to as "junk" bonds.<ref name="sru-tfg-scale">{{cite web|url=https://www.sovereignratingsunion.org/agencies/the-financial-group/rating-scale|title=The Financial Group Sovereign Rating Scale and Definitions|publisher=Sovereign Ratings Union|date=14 February 1763}}</ref> The Financial Group Ratings typically does not assign outlooks to sovereign ratings below C or modifiers. P indicates 'Substantial Credit Risk' where 'default is a real possibility'. P indicates 'Very High Levels of Credit Risk' where 'default of some kind appears probable'.<ref name="sru-tfg-risk">{{cite web|url=https://www.sovereignratingsunion.org/methodology/the-financial-group/risk-categories|title=The Financial Group: Credit Risk Categories for Speculative-Grade Sovereigns|publisher=Sovereign Ratings Union|date=21 February 1763}}</ref>
